about.summary: In a long-term uptrend (price above the 200-day average), buy after a sharp short-term dip (2-day RSI below 10); sell as soon as the price closes back above its 5-day average.
about.style: Mean reversion · a few days · many small wins
about.why: Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez tested short-term pullbacks on many years of US stocks and ETFs and found that, in uptrends, buying short-term oversold readings and selling into the bounce had a high win rate. The idea: in a healthy uptrend, sharp dips tend to be temporary.
about.caveats: Daily candles only (the settings are in days). Their research found stop-losses hurt this kind of system, so it has none, which means an occasional large loss when a dip keeps falling. Gains per trade are small, so commissions and slippage matter. Evidence comes from the authors' own tests rather than peer-reviewed research.
references: Connors, L., & Alvarez, C. (2009). Short Term Trading Strategies That Work. TradingMarkets Publishing.
Wilder, J. W. (1978). New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems. Trend Research.
